name: FIFA 11+ Injury Prevention Warm-up (Level 2)
description: The intermediate version of FIFA's 20-minute injury-prevention warm-up: the same running drills, with harder planks, partner Nordics, walking lunges, partner throwing balance and lateral jumps.
whoItsFor: Soccer players aged 14+ who have done Level 1 cleanly for about 4 weeks and want to keep cutting knee, ankle, hamstring and groin injury risk. Done on the pitch with a partner and a ball.
howToRun: Start of every training session, at least twice a week, in this order: Part 1, Part 2, Part 3.
Move here from Level 1 when every exercise is done with good technique; each level takes about 4 weeks to master.
Before matches do only the running parts (Parts 1 and 3) - the strength block is not done pre-match.
Knees never buckle inwards on squats, lunges or landings; keep the pelvis level on single-leg work.

exercises.name: Running - straight ahead (6-10 cone pairs, 5-6 m apart)
Running - hip out
Running - hip in
Running - circling partner
Running - shoulder contact jumps
Running - quick forwards & backwards
The bench - alternate legs (hold each lift 2 s)
Sideways bench - raise & lower hip
Nordic hamstrings - intermediate (partner holds ankles)
Single-leg stance - throwing ball with partner (2-3 m apart)
Squats - walking lunges
Jumping - lateral jumps (about 1 m side to side)
Running across the pitch
Bounding
Plant & cut

credit: FIFA Medical Assessment and Research Centre (F-MARC)

name: FIFA 11+ Injury Prevention Warm-up (Level 3)
description: The advanced level of FIFA's injury-prevention warm-up: one-leg plank holds, side plank with leg lift, 12-15 Nordics, partner push balance, one-leg squats and explosive multi-direction box jumps.
whoItsFor: Experienced soccer players (14+) who have mastered Level 2 and want the hardest version of the 11+ inside their normal warm-up time.
howToRun: Start of every training session, at least twice a week, in this order: Part 1, Part 2, Part 3.
Only progress here after about 4 weeks of clean Level 2 work; it is fine to be on Level 3 for one exercise and Level 2 for another.
Before matches do only Parts 1 and 3.
If Nordic or one-leg squat technique breaks down, drop back a level for that exercise.

Running - hip out
Running - hip in
Running - circling partner
Running - shoulder contact jumps
Running - quick forwards & backwards
The bench - one leg lift & hold (10-15 cm)
Sideways bench - with leg lift
Nordic hamstrings - advanced (partner holds ankles)
Single-leg stance - test your partner (push off balance)
Squats - one-leg squats (hold partner lightly)
Jumping - box jumps (across an imaginary cross)
Running across the pitch
Bounding

name: FIFA 11+ for Kids (Level 1)
description: FIFA's injury-prevention warm-up for 7-13 year olds, level 1: a stop-on-one-leg running game, landing practice, partner throwing balance, a press-up tunnel, one-leg jumps, a spider-position ball drill and learning to fall and roll safely.
whoItsFor: Children aged 7-13 at club or school football. Needs a coach calling commands, one ball per player and a space from penalty-area to half-pitch size. Players over 14 use the adult 11+.
howToRun: Replaces the normal warm-up at the start of every training session (at least twice a week); takes 15-20 minutes once learned.
Do the 7 exercises in this order - the manual says the order should not change.
Move a child up a level for an exercise only when they do it correctly over several sessions; levels are never skipped and children can be on different levels for different exercises.
Leave plenty of space between players for the jumps and rolls; wait at least 5 s between rolls.

exercises.name: Alertness running game - listen for the stop command (stand on one leg 3 s)
Skating jumps - learning how to land (hold 3 s)
Single-leg stance - throwing the ball with a partner
Press-ups - tunnel (press-up position, max 8 per group)
Single-leg jumps - forwards (hold 3 s)
Spiderman - stroking the ball
Sideways roll - from squatting position

name: FIFA 11+ for Kids (Level 3)
description: Level 3 of FIFA 11+ for Kids: the running game with a ball in the hands, one-hand ball balance on landing, a one-leg passing game, rolling the ball around the hands in press-up position, sideways one-leg jumps, the crab walk and rolls from standing.
whoItsFor: Children aged 7-13 at club or school football. Needs a coach calling commands, one ball per player and a space from penalty-area to half-pitch size. Players over 14 use the adult 11+.
howToRun: Replaces the normal warm-up at the start of every training session (at least twice a week); takes 15-20 minutes once learned.
Do the 7 exercises in this order - the manual says the order should not change.
Move a child up a level for an exercise only when they do it correctly over several sessions; levels are never skipped and children can be on different levels for different exercises.
Leave plenty of space between players for the jumps and rolls; wait at least 5 s between rolls.

exercises.name: Alertness running game - ball in the hands, listen for the stop command
Skating jumps - balancing with the ball in one hand
Single-leg stance - passing game (instep pass and stop)
Press-ups - rolling the ball around the hands (figure eight)
Single-leg jumps - sideways (coach gives direction)
Spiderman - the crab (on all fours, feet first)
Sideways roll - dynamically from a standing position

name: FIFA 11+ for Kids (Level 5)
description: The top level of FIFA 11+ for Kids: dribbling into one-leg stops, dynamic balance reaches with the ball, a partner push-balance game, press-up holds on the ball, one-leg jumps in any direction holding a ball, 'ball bearing' spider walks and rolls from a jog.
whoItsFor: Children aged 7-13 at club or school football. Needs a coach calling commands, one ball per player and a space from penalty-area to half-pitch size. Players over 14 use the adult 11+. Level 5 is for children who have mastered levels 1-4.
howToRun: Replaces the normal warm-up at the start of every training session (at least twice a week); takes 15-20 minutes once learned.
Do the 7 exercises in this order - the manual says the order should not change.
Move a child up a level for an exercise only when they do it correctly over several sessions; levels are never skipped and children can be on different levels for different exercises.
Leave plenty of space between players for the jumps and rolls; wait at least 5 s between rolls.

Skating jumps - dynamic balancing with ball (reach ball forward, leg back)
Single-leg stance - testing the partner's balance (balls pressed together)
Press-ups - hands on the ball (walk feet back and forth)
Single-leg jumps - coach indicates direction, ball in both hands
Spiderman - ball bearing (roll ball under feet)

name: IABA School of Boxing + Bodyweight Circuit
description: Six themed shadow-boxing rounds (defence-only movement, back-foot boxing, feint-and-counter, jab ladders, close-range pressure, open round) followed by a 4-set bodyweight circuit on a 30 s on, 5 s off clock.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move.
howToRun: Use 3-minute rounds (2-minute for juniors) with 1 minute rest; visualise an opponent every round.
Keep rounds 1, 5 and 6 at 50-70% effort as written - the quality of movement is the point.
The circuit is 8 moves x 30 s with a 5 s change-over, all bodyweight; rest 1-2 minutes between the 4 sets.
Rest times between rounds and circuit sets are not given by the IABA here - 1 minute and 1-2 minutes are sensible defaults.

exercises.name: Warm-up: general warm-up and stretch
Shadow round 1: movement only, defence (60-70%, no punches)
Shadow round 2: back-foot boxing, single defensive shots
Shadow round 3: lead feint, step off, back-hand attack (1-2 punches)
Shadow round 4: full-extension jab ladder (1-2-3 jabs forward and back)
Shadow round 5: close-range pressure, no punching, cut off angles
Shadow round 6: open round, all ranges (60-70%)
Lunges
Press-ups
Tuck jumps
Sit-ups
Squats
Plank
Leg raises (up and down)
Ankle grabs

name: IABA Counter-Attack Rounds + Skipping Ladder
description: A long technical session: 6 school-of-boxing shadow rounds, then 8 counter-attack rounds (jabs, slips, blocks, side steps, shifts, step-backs, lean-backs) and a 5-minute skipping ladder from 50% to flat out.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move. Best for boxers who already shadow box comfortably for 6+ rounds.
howToRun: School-of-boxing rounds: 3 min (juniors 2 min) with 1 minute rest; sip water between rounds.
Counter-attack rounds: follow the rep counts in each round (x5 each), then rest 2 minutes before skipping.
Skip 5 minutes without stopping, lifting the pace every minute: 50, 60, 70, 80, then 100%.
Cool down with 5 minutes light skipping and 15 minutes of stretching, rolling any problem areas.

exercises.name: Warm-up
Stretch
School of boxing: shadow rounds (defence, feints, attacks)
Counter round 1: from front station - jab x5, back hand x5, 2-1 x5
Counter round 2: same as round 1, after slips
Counter round 3: slip in, close distance, up to 3 punches (x5 each side)
Counter round 4: after blocks, 1-3 punches of choice
Counter round 5: side step x5, shifts x5, then up to 3 punches after each defence
Counter round 6: step back + counter defence, 1-3 punches each side
Counter round 7: step back with same-time punch, rotating sides
Counter round 8: after lean back, 1-3 punches both hands (x5)
Rest
Skipping ladder (50-60-70-80-100%, 1 min each, no break)
Recovery
Cool-down: light skipping
Stretch and roll (feet to head)

name: IABA School of Boxing + Shuttle Sprints
description: Six shadow rounds (defence-only movement, high-tempo feints, lead-hand feints, second-phase combos, close-range pressure, open round), then 25 m shuttle sprints with jog-back recovery and a short press-up, sit-up and squat-thrust finisher.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move. Needs about 25 m of safe running space for the sprints.
howToRun: Shadow rounds 3 min (juniors 2 min) with about 1 minute rest.
Warm up the legs well before sprinting; sprint the 25 m flat out and jog slowly back as the recovery, letting your breathing settle before the next one.
Youths do 5 sets of 5 sprints, juniors 5 sets of 4 (the page writes '5 x 5 sets' / '5 x 4 sets').
Core finisher 3 x 15 of each; stretch afterwards.

exercises.name: Warm-up: general warm-up and stretch
Shadow round 1: movement only at 50%, defence
Shadow round 2: high-tempo movement and feints only
Shadow round 3: lead hand only - feint head/throw body, feint body/throw head
Shadow round 4: 2nd-phase combos - draw, slip/step, return 2-3 punches
Shadow round 5: close range - short hooks and uppercuts, high guard
Shadow round 6: open round, all ranges (60-70%)
Shuttle sprint, jog back recovery
Press-ups
Sit-ups
Squat thrusts

name: IABA Technical Rounds, Skipping & Planks
description: Six technical shadow rounds on a short 30 s rest (lead hand only, back hand only, spin-offs, rolls, uppercut/hook leads, open round), then 6 x 3-minute skipping rounds with a 10 s sprint finish each minute and 5 x 1-minute front planks.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move.
howToRun: Technical rounds 3 min (juniors 2 min) with only 30 s rest - then a full 3-minute break.
Skipping: 50 s medium pace then 10 s as fast as you can, repeated through each 3-minute round, 1 minute rest between rounds.
Front plank: forearms down, elbows under shoulders, legs together, back flat; 30 s between holds.
Finish with a 10-minute cool-down stretch.

exercises.name: Warm-up: general warm-up and stretching
Technical round 1: lead hand only, any distance (back hand defends)
Technical round 2: back hand only, any distance
Technical round 3: 3-4 punch combos at long range, turn/spin off every 15 s
Technical round 4: 3-4 punch combos at short range, roll out every 15 s
Technical round 5: 2-3 shot combos led by uppercut or hook
Technical round 6: open round, correct technique at high pace
Rest
Skipping rounds (50 s medium + 10 s max, repeat)
Front plank
Cool-down stretch

name: IABA Shadow Rounds: Feints & Counters
description: Six detailed shadow rounds built around shape and feints: movement-only, long-range feints, feints into mid-range uppercut counters, side-step attacks, defence-then-counter and a free round, finished with 10 minutes of light skipping.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move.
howToRun: Morning session; pair it with the IABA run + circuit + planks session later the same day, or do it on its own.
Rounds 3 min (juniors 2 min) with 1 minute rest; sip water between rounds.
Hands high and elbows tucked through every round; mix the two patterns in the last 30 s of rounds 2 and 3.
Cool down with 10 minutes of light skipping and 10 minutes of full-body stretching.

exercises.name: Warm-up
Stretch
Round 1: shape, movement, slips/ducks/rolls and feints - no punching
Round 2: long-range feints (show lead, body back hand; show back hand, lead to head)
Round 3: feints with mid-range uppercut counters, finish with explosive hook
Round 4: side-step with same-time punch, add straight shot then back-hand hooks
Round 5: step back + counter defence, then 3-4 punches head and body
Round 6: free round - attack, defence, guard, movement
Cool-down: light skipping
Full-body stretch

name: IABA Run, Power Circuit & Plank Series
description: Boxing S&C at home: 20 minutes running at a good pace, two rounds of a 7-station circuit (30 reps each of star jumps, paused squats, push-ups, sit-ups, tuck jumps, Russian twists, burpees) and a 6-minute front and side plank series.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness trainees who want a no-equipment strength-endurance session. Written for the IABA youth and junior squads, so expect it to be hard; scale reps down if 30 is too many.
howToRun: Afternoon session paired with the IABA feints & counters shadow rounds, or on its own on a conditioning day.
Run 20 minutes at a good, steady pace before the circuit.
Circuit: 15 s between stations, 2 minutes between the two circuits.
Plank series with 30 s between stations; cool down with 5 minutes light skipping or jogging on the spot and 10 minutes of stretching.

exercises.name: Warm-up: general warm-up and stretch
Run at a good pace
Explosive star jumps
Squats with 3 s hold at the bottom
Push-ups
Sit-ups
Tuck jumps (knees to chest)
Russian twists
Burpees
Front plank
Left side plank with arm raises
Right side plank with arm raises
Front plank rising to full arms (alternate)
Front plank with alternate leg raise
Side plank with top-leg raises (30 s each side, no rest)
Cool-down: light skipping or jog on the spot
Stretch (feet to head)

name: IABA Shadow Boxing Rounds + Skipping Ladder
description: A school-of-boxing session that builds from footwork and defence to counters off slips and blocks, an intense close-range round and a hard free round, then 2 x 5 minutes of skipping that gets faster each minute.
whoItsFor: Amateur boxers and boxing-fit trainees who know their stance, guard and basic punches. Written for Ireland's youth and junior national squads, so it suits experienced juniors and adults. No partner or bag needed - just space to move.
howToRun: Dynamic warm-up 12 minutes plus a 3-minute stretch.
Rounds 3 min (juniors 2 min) with 1 minute rest; the page sets 7 rounds but describes six - do the six below, adding a seventh free round only if you are used to 7.
Skipping: two 5-minute blocks, starting light and lifting speed every minute.
Cool down and stretch for 10 minutes. Pair with the IABA core session the same day if you want a double.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up
Stretch
Round 1: footwork and defence only, build intensity
Round 2: open round - 1-4 punch combos, then defence + double attack
Round 3: counters - slip and close distance, 1-4 punches
Round 4: counters off blocks - 1-3 punches, then block + double attack
Round 5: intense close range - hooks, uppercuts, body-head shifts
Round 6: free round with intensity and power
Skipping, light then faster each minute
Cool-down and stretch

name: IABA Run + Boxer's Core Series
description: A 60-minute S&C session: 20 minutes running at a good pace, then two rounds of a 10-exercise floor core series (sit-ups, crunch pulses, rotations, side sways, elbow-to-knee, leg holds, criss-cross, supermans) and a long stretch.
whoItsFor: Boxers and anyone wanting a tough no-equipment run-and-core session. Written for the IABA youth and junior squads.
howToRun: Warm up for 10 minutes, then run 20 minutes at a good pace and recover for 3 minutes.
Core series: knees bent hip-width, neck neutral ('an apple between chin and chest'); do the list once, rest 2 minutes, repeat.
Jog lightly on the spot with arm crosses and trunk twists for 5 minutes after the core work.
Stretch for 10 minutes, rolling any tight spots.

exercises.name: Warm-up: general warm-up and stretch
Run at a good pace
Recovery
Sit-ups, knees bent
Crunches with finger slide and 1-inch pulse
Bent-leg crunch, push arms between legs
Sit-up with hands rotating outside alternate legs
Low side sways (touch sides of feet)
Elbow to opposite knee
Leg hold 15 cm off floor, open and close
Leg criss-cross 15 cm off floor
Criss-cross with leg rise, 4-count
Superman hold (3 s)
Light jog on the spot with arm crosses and trunk twists
Full-body stretch with roller

name: England Boxing Skipping Rounds
description: Three skipping rounds that rotate normal skipping, high knees, cross-overs and double unders every 10 seconds in a different order each round, to mimic the changing pace of a bout.
whoItsFor: Boxers and boxing-fitness beginners who can already skip steadily for a minute. Rounds are 1.5 min for schools-age, 2 min for juniors and 3 min for youths and seniors. Use double unders only once you can do them; otherwise swap in fast singles.
howToRun: Warm up for a few minutes first, with suitable footwear on a safe, non-slip surface.
Each round: change the skill every 10 s and keep cycling the four skills until the bell.
Rest about 1 minute between rounds (England Boxing does not state the rest).
Use it as a finisher after shadow or bag work, or as a short stand-alone session.

exercises.name: Warm-up: easy skipping and mobility
Round 1: normal - high knees - cross-overs - double unders (10 s each, repeat)
Round 2: high knees - cross-overs - double unders - normal (10 s each, repeat)
Round 3: cross-overs - double unders - normal - high knees (10 s each, repeat)
